title: Four levels of protein structure
caption: Each level builds on the one before. The sequence (primary) decides which hydrogen bonds form along the backbone (secondary), how the R groups fold the chain (tertiary), and, for proteins with several chains, how the subunits fit together (quaternary).
alt: Four boxes in order: primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure, each with the bonds that hold it.
description: Primary structure: the order of amino acids, joined by peptide bonds, from the amino end to the carboxyl end.
Secondary structure: α-helices and β-sheets: hydrogen bonds between backbone C=O and N–H groups.
Tertiary structure: the 3D fold of one chain: hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, disulfide bridges and hydrophobic interactions between R groups.
Quaternary structure: two or more chains together, as in haemoglobin (four subunits).
Not every protein has a quaternary structure: only those made of more than one chain.
